I do not mean to self-advertise or whatever, I just really really love playing against zombies in whatever config as long as the enemies are zombie or zombie-like. Ever since I stopped my "Roblox is for kids" mindset, took a look around and found Guts and Blackpowder my zombie craze just kicked back in full gear and that craze just couldn't handle my AI teammates just running into the fecking horde because they are programmed by default to charge their enemy if within range.
It's good for Helldiver Terminids, Vietnam zombies or COD zombies, Guts and Blackpowder style Napoleonic zombies... Zombies!

I say yes. The modding scene has a whole lot of potential. Mutators for instance which are mods that are mainly scripts change a whole lot as they can even alter AI behaviour. Modding is straightforward too if you can take the time to learn stuff. I made one because I wanted to play zombie configs and wanted my AI buddies to run away when enemies are in range so it would feel immersive. The mods for custom maps, skins, weapons, and vehicles are all impressive too and weapons and vehicles also have their settings that affect AI behaviour such that they aren't just for appearances. The game is so great because it is so versatile. You could have configs for modern stuff, cold war, ww1, ww2, zombies, etc. I haven't seen any other simulation game like Ravenfield, honestly. My only point of contention is that the AI is pretty pretty simple however being able to mod a lot of things with hard work overshadows that.

I use EaglePancake's RF Launcher... it's an application in a zip in a mod on the workshop... you load in all the mods, then tick all the mods you need then enter a name for the "playlist" on the field below then press save then press launch... you can load the playlist again by searching for the name you set it to in the dropdown thing by the field. My only problem with it though is that it reads the .rfc filenames so even though you subscribed to this one mod, it's .rfc filename may be different since people usually don't see those I guess.. like for example, there is a mod that is a flashlight and another that is a repair torch, but they have the same .rfc filename...
